Why I buy LEAP Calls Over 3x ETFs $NVDA $TSLA

I’ve seen a lot of people ask why I prefer LEAP calls over 3x ETFs.

📌 Both experience decay, but here’s the key difference:

✅ LEAPs have steady time decay (theta), which is predictable.

❌ 3x ETFs can compound decay over time, eroding value even if the stock stays flat.

In the long run, 3x ETFs can bleed out faster, making LEAPs the safer choice for longer-term plays.

Even after nearly a decade of trading, I still make mistakes. Here’s one that cost me—and how I’m fixing it $TSLA 

Over the past few weeks one of my biggest mistakes has been entering trades based on extreme discounts instead of waiting for the daily BX and eventually the weekly BX to confirm higher lows. 

Buying deep discounts can work for high-risk high-reward setups but our edge in 2024 came from waiting for confirmation not just chasing the biggest risk-reward plays.

Moving forward I’m only entering trades when the daily BX forms higher lows, followed by the weekly BX confirming the trend. This would have saved a lot of short-term pain since I’ve been too focused on bot signals, which rely mainly on the 11 SMA instead of full confirmation.

#️⃣ 1hr-swing-bot-alerts is great, but it’s even better when it lines up with a bottom on the daily BX.

A perfect example is Tesla, where we could’ve entered on the first higher low on the daily BX, but instead it just broke higher without us. Now we’re looking to re-enter today at a much better price and likely ride it back up to $350 before another potential rejection.

I’m sharing this with you because even after nearly a decade of doing this I’m still human and far from perfect, so don’t worry if you are too.

This type of discipline is gonna be even more important if we head into a bear market for the rest of 2025.
